status_assessment.basis: The parish's own website (Anglican Life Rangiora) lists St Martin's Loburn as 'Closed' on its home page and service page, and says the congregation now meets at St John's Rangiora. No service times are given for Loburn. Neither page is dated, the service page confuses the name with St Matthew's, and I found no dated closure notice, final service, deconsecration or sale. So the church is assessed as likely inactive rather than confirmed inactive. The diocesan Anglican Life directory still lists the church, but the entry is undated and gives no services.
status_assessment.osm_stale_basis: The current OSM version (v4, 2024-12-07) still tags the way amenity=place_of_worship with service_times=Su[1,3,4] 10:00 and links a defunct generic website (anglicanweb.org). The parish says the church is closed. No OSM edit reflects the closure, for example a disused: or was: lifecycle prefix or the removal of service_times.

run_manifest.notes: claude session 061c70a9-e585-48cd-add2-e12240ef5ad5; num_turns 22; permission_denials 0 | The strongest evidence of closure is the parish's own website, which is undated. Its service page for St Martin's - Loburn has the status 'Closed', but the body text says 'Since the closing of St. Matthew's Loburn church'. St Matthew's is the parish's Fernside centre, which is still listed with services, so the body text is probably a copy error. A reviewer should confirm the closure date, and whether the building has been deconsecrated or disposed of, with the parish or diocese, or from Anglican Life news items. I could not reach three sources: Papers Past search returned no readable content, DigitalNZ and the Canterbury Stories photo record returned 403, and the Waimakariri Heritage (recollect) record returned 403. As a result I found no contemporary 1891 newspaper report of the opening or consecration. The Waimakariri Libraries history page is not on the allowlist; it is a council library site and is treated here as secondary. Search-engine summaries mentioned an August 2024 'active' listing and a 1st/3rd/4th Sunday pattern with Communion, but I did not open pages carrying that text, and they are not cited. A vicar's name and a phone number on the diocesan and OSM records were deliberately left out.
